title: Multi-type settings validation can raise AttributeError instead of ValidationError
reasoning: Several settings rules pass a tuple of expected types such as (int, float) into validate_field. On type mismatch, validate_field formats expected_type.__name__, but tuples do not have __name__, so invalid numeric settings can escape the intended ValidationError path as AttributeError. The included test only exercises a single expected type, so it does not catch the tuple branch.
reproduction: Call validate_settings_update_field(key="llm_timeout", value="bad", validate_field=validate_field) or validate_settings_update({"llm_timeout": "bad"}); the mismatch path attempts expected_type.__name__ on a tuple.
recommendation: Make validate_field format tuple expected types safely, for example by joining each type.__name__, and keep raising the custom ValidationError for mismatches.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only expected-type test uses browser_automation_enabled, whose rule has a single bool type, so expected_type.__name__ exists.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that validates a tuple-typed key such as llm_timeout with an invalid string value and asserts a ValidationError with a useful message, not AttributeError.
minimumFixScope: Update validate_field's type-name formatting for tuple expected_type values and add focused coverage for a tuple-typed settings rule.
